title: 3 programming languages that will die by 2028

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: By 2028, COBOL, Fortran, and Lisp will be extinct — outdated, unsupported, and irrelevant in modern tech stacks.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Programming isn't dying — it's evolving. Python, Rust, and JavaScript dominate because they adapt to new paradigms and hardware.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: COBOL still powers 80% of global banking systems. Fortran remains in scientific computing. Lisp's macro system is unmatched for AI research.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Legacy systems can't sustain growth. Modern languages offer concurrency, memory safety, and ecosystem support — essential for AI and quantum computing.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Programming thrives because it's the foundation of innovation — not a relic of the past.
